title: Contract amendment approval criteria, billing cutoff windows, and revenue-trigger guidance
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This page defines the approval criteria, billing cutoff practices, and revenue recognition triggers for contract amendments, change orders, and supplier-side modifications that materially affect pricing, term, or deliverables. It bridges Legal, Finance, Procurement, and Revenue teams to ensure consistent accounting treatment and forecasting updates. Use this guidance for: amendments, scope changes, early terminations, material waivers, and pricing/discount adjustments.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to all contracts where Redwood Inference is a party and the amendment impacts one or more of the following: billed consideration, billing cadence, service start/end dates, material deliverables, or termination/exit economics.
- Does not replace sector-specific procurement Master Service Agreements (MSAs) when those documents contain explicit, higher-priority operational clauses; in such cases follow MSA instructions and record deviation reasons.

Definitions

- Amendment: any written change to an existing contract that modifies price, term, scope, or billing.
- Change order: customer-initiated addendum that increases or decreases contracted units or features.
- Billing cutoff window: defined processing window at month-end when billing runs are locked for invoicing and revenue recognition.
- Revenue trigger: the contractual event that changes the timing or pattern of revenue recognition (e.g., billing start date, milestone acceptance, service commencement).

Principles

1) Single source of truth: all amendments must be recorded in the contract repository with a unique amendment ID and tagged with the accounting treatment code.
2) Timely signaling: Procurement or Sales must notify Finance at least 10 business days prior to a scheduled billing run for amendments that affect revenue in the upcoming period.
3) Materiality thresholding: only amendments which meet materiality thresholds (monetary or operational) require the full multi-team approval path; non-material edits use an expedited workflow.
4) Clear ownership: Legal shepherds contract wording; Finance owns accounting treatment and revenue recognition decisions; Procurement enforces supplier obligations; Sales/CS executes customer-side communications.

Materiality thresholds

- Monetary materiality: any amendment increasing or decreasing ARR/committed consideration by >= $50,000 annually or changing one-time fees >= $25,000 requires full review.
- Timing materiality: any change that shifts recognition across fiscal months or quarters (e.g., moves revenue from Q4 to Q1) requires escalation regardless of dollar value.
- Operational materiality: changes that modify termination economics, data-residency, or SLA credits are material.

Approval matrix (summary)

- Minor edits (non-financial wording, contact details): Legal approval only.
- Non-material financial edits (below monetary threshold and no timing change): Legal + Procurement sign-off; Finance notified.
- Material amendments: Legal + Finance + Procurement + Sales/GTM director approval. If amendment impacts revenue recognition timing, CFO or delegated revenue manager must sign-off.

Step-by-step amendment processing (standard flow)

1) Draft amendment created in Contract Repository (CR) with amendment ID and short description.
2) Originator selects amendment type, estimates financial impact, and tags affected fiscal periods.
3) Legal performs clause-level review and produces final amendment language.
4) Procurement or Sales completes the Amendment Impact Form (AIF) that includes: effective date, billing change, termination change, discounting, and forecast delta.
5) Finance receives AIF and performs initial accounting assessment within 3 business days. Assessment outputs: accounting treatment code (deferral/proration/milestone), required journal entries, and revenue timing impact.
6) Approvals collected per the Approval Matrix. Electronic approvals via the contract system count as signatures.
7) Once approved, the amendment is executed and tagged in the CR; Billing and Revenue runbooks are queued for the next billing cutoff window.

Billing cutoff windows and operational rules

- Standard monthly cutoff: Billing cutoff occurs at 18:00 UTC on the last business day of the month. All billing-impacting amendments must be fully executed and recorded in the CR before this cutoff to appear on that month’s invoices.
- Extended cutoff for EMEA/APAC close: For global deals impacting multiple regions, an alternate cutoff of 20:00 UTC on the last business day is available if Finance is notified 5 business days in advance.
- Emergency mid-cycle adjustments: Emergency waivers that must invoice mid-period require a documented Emergency Billing Request with CFO delegate approval and will be processed outside standard batch runs; these are logged for audit.

Proration and credit/charge handling

- Monthly subscriptions: When an amendment changes seat counts or unit quantities mid-month, billing is prorated by calendar days using the formula: prorated_amount = (daily_rate x days_active).
- One-time fees: Apply to the invoice covering the effective date, unless the amendment explicitly defers the fee via a signed deferral agreement.
- Credits and retroactive discounts: Must be applied using a credit invoice referencing the original invoice ID; any credit > $5,000 requires Budget Owner approval.

Revenue recognition treatment mapping (quick reference table)

Type of amendment | Typical accounting treatment | Who approves accounting code
------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------
Price increase/decrease (ongoing) | Prospective billing change; recognize revenue as billed unless performance obligations change | Finance (Revenue Manager)
Term extension without price change | No immediate revenue change; update forecast and disclosure | Finance
Term extension with prepaid payment | Defer recognition and amortize over extended term | Finance + Revenue Manager
Milestone or deliverable addition | Milestone accounting: recognize on milestone satisfaction | Finance + Controller
Termination with settlement | Recognize settlement as one-time revenue (or loss) per legal terms; may need impairment | Finance + CFO

Accounting assessment playbook (short)

- Step A: Identify performance obligations impacted. Document whether amendment creates new obligations or modifies existing ones.
- Step B: Determine consideration promised and allocation method. Apply existing allocation unless amendment specifies a change.
- Step C: Compute recognition pattern: immediate, over time (amortized), or milestone-based.
- Step D: Prepare proposed journal entries and communicate with Close team 5 business days before period close.

Checklist for Legal, Finance, Procurement (pre-approval)

- Legal: amendment language, signatures, amendment ID, cross-reference to original SOW/MSA.
- Finance: AIF completed, accounting treatment code, affected GL buckets, forecast delta, required JE templates.
- Procurement: Supplier-side confirmation (if supplier is involved), PO updates, spend approvals.
- Sales/CS: Customer notification template, billing notice timeline, renewal calendar updates.

Sample amendment clause snippets (for template reuse)

1) Effective date and billing: "This Amendment is effective as of [DATE]. Billing for the change will commence on [BILLING_START_DATE] and will be reflected on the invoice cycle following execution in accordance with Redwood Inference's standard billing practices."

2) One-time fee deferral: "Customer and Redwood agree that the one-time implementation fee of $[AMOUNT] shall be invoiced on execution and deferred for accounting purposes to be recognized over the period of [TERM] months, starting on [RECOGNITION_START_DATE]."

3) Retroactive pricing: "Any retroactive price adjustments requested after an invoice has been issued will be handled via a credit memo referencing the original invoice. Retroactive credits in excess of $[THRESHOLD] require Finance approval prior to issuance."

Integration with forecasting and budgeting

- Forecast signal: Approved amendments that affect committed consideration must be reflected in the ARR/TCV forecast workbook within 2 business days of approval. The originator must supply the updated ARR delta and the fiscal impact by period.
- Procurement alignment: Purchase orders and committed spend schedules must be updated to reflect amended terms to avoid procurement-to-pay mismatches.
- Reforecast cadence: Significant amendments (per materiality) trigger an immediate reforecast and, if crossing quarters, require a short memo to FP&A describing revenue timing changes.

Escalation and exceptions

- If Finance and Legal disagree on recognition treatment, escalate to the Revenue Manager and Controller for a binding decision.
- Exceptions to cutoff windows are rare and require documentation, rationale, and CFO delegate sign-off. Workflow exceptions are logged for post-close audit.

Audit and retention

- All amendment records, AIFs, approvals, and resulting JE templates must be retained in the contract repository and the finance document retention system for 7 years.
- Quarterly internal audits will sample 10% of amendments flagged as material to validate that the approved accounting treatment was applied.

Operational examples (two scenarios)

Scenario A — Seat increase mid-month (non-material): Customer adds 10 seats on 2026-01-12 for subscription at $100/month. Action: Sales creates AIF, Legal issues amendment, Finance approves proration. Billing: prorated invoice issued at next monthly run (prorated days). Forecast: ARR delta applied prospectively. Approvals: Legal + Procurement sign-off.

Scenario B — Prepaid term extension with one-time settlement (material): Customer prepays $180,000 on 2026-01-20 to extend a multi-year commitment. Action: AIF triggers Finance accounting code for deferral/amortization over 24 months. Approvals: Legal + Finance + CFO delegate. Billing: invoice issued upon execution; revenue recognized monthly per amortization schedule starting 2026-02-01. Forecast: immediate TCV update; ARR recognition per amortization.
